prompt: Generate reproducible passwords that always contain a lowercase letter, an uppercase letter and a digit, then write the validator that proves it. Complete the generate and satisfiesRule methods in the starter file.
explanation: Guaranteeing a character-class rule is easiest by construction: place one character from each required class first, fill the rest from the combined pool, then shuffle so the guaranteed characters are not stuck at the front. Because the shuffle draws from the same seeded Random, the password is a pure function of length and seed, which is what lets the tests hard-code expected strings. satisfiesRule then verifies the property independently, so the generator is checked against the rule rather than against itself.
hints: Build the password in a char[] so you can shuffle it in place before turning it into a String.
The first three slots come from LOWER, UPPER and DIGITS in that order; slots 3 and up come from the 62-character POOL.
The shuffle is Fisher-Yates over the whole array: for i from length - 1 down to 1, swap out[i] with out[rng.nextInt(i + 1)].
